title: For a flat qcqs morphism the coherator and derived pushforward commute: RQ_Y Rf_* = Phi RQ_X

standard_prerequisites.name: Pushforward preserves quasi-coherence for qcqs morphisms
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes f_*I-bullet quasi-coherent for K-injective I-bullet in QCoh.

standard_prerequisites.name: QCoh is a Grothendieck abelian category with enough K-injectives
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Properties, proposition coherator; Injectives, theorem K-injective-embedding-grothendieck (cross-chapter, named)
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the K-injective resolution defining Phi.

standard_prerequisites.name: Adjunctions for the derived functors
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cohomology, lemma adjoint; Derived Categories, lemma derived-adjoint-functors (cross-chapter, named)
standard_prerequisites.use: Give f^* right-adjoint to Rf_* on D(O) and to Phi on D(QCoh).

core_obligations: Define Phi on D(QCoh(O_X)) as f_* of a K-injective complex of quasi-coherent modules (well-defined by the K-injective embedding theorem).
Flatness makes f^* exact, so f^* defines functors D(O_Y) -> D(O_X) and D(QCoh(O_Y)) -> D(QCoh(O_X)).
Establish the two adjunction pairs: f^* adjoint to Rf_* on D(O), and f^* adjoint to Phi on D(QCoh) via the derived adjoint functors lemma.
Compute for A in D(QCoh(O_Y)), E in D(O_X) the four-term Hom chain Hom(A, RQ_Y Rf_*E) = Hom(A, Rf_*E) = Hom(f^*A, E) = Hom(f^*A, RQ_X E) = Hom(A, Phi RQ_X E).
Conclude both composites are right adjoint to the same functor, hence canonically isomorphic.
proof_roadmap: K-injective definition of Phi; exactness of f^*; two adjunction pairs; four-term Hom computation; adjoint-uniqueness conclusion.
difficulty_reason: A right-adjoint uniqueness argument; the content is the two adjunction pairs and the four-term Hom chain.
